headline: Prince William Launches Free Tool to Help Communities Weather Emergencies
meta_description: Prince William launches Ready Together, a free online toolkit helping UK communities prepare for floods, wildfires and other emergencies through practical plan…
summary_short: Prince William has launched Ready Together, a free initiative designed to help communities across the UK build resilience and prepare for emergencies like floods and wil…
body:
Prince William has launched Ready Together, a National Emergencies Trust initiative offering a free online toolkit to help communities prepare for emergencies ranging from floods and wildfires to power cuts and cyber attacks. Developed with researchers at Nottingham Trent University, the toolkit guides community groups—from residents' associations to sports clubs—through eight areas of emergency preparedness, including communications, supplies, and supporting vulnerable residents. Groups can identify local skills and resources, plan for potential crises, and create shareable emergency plans. The prince, who serves as patron of the charity, unveiled the initiative in Ilminster, Somerset, a town that has weathered both severe flooding nine years ago and more recent wildfires.

The launch came during a visit where Prince William met 74-year-old Tina Groves, a visually impaired resident whose home was inundated during those floods. Her neighbours helped rescue her and rebuild her home—a demonstration of community resilience that inspired the initiative's focus on mutual aid. "It's the sort of thing that nobody thinks about; when you have difficulties seeing, how a flooding event might affect you," the prince reflected, highlighting how preparedness requires understanding diverse needs.

Actor Ross Kemp, an ambassador for Ready Together, emphasised that while professional emergency services are vital, communities are "usually the first in and the last out" during crises. His reporting from disaster zones prompted him to keep emergency supplies at home—tinned food, batteries, candles—advice now embedded in the toolkit. The guidance acknowledges real constraints too; recommending cash reserves carries challenges during a cost of living crisis. Yet the evidence is compelling: according to Our World in Data, the global death rate from disasters has fallen more than 90% over the past century, despite population growth, largely through better preparedness and warning systems. Ready Together aims to extend that protective effect to every community willing to plan ahead.
